page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading and dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is equipped with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25% at 2931.08. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth remain in the average tier, with read-only large block bandwidth at 68.67 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 49.73 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates average performance across standard workloads, including software compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving throughput at 10.6 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, placing in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-highcpu-8 offers a resource-dense profile for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores provide reliable execution without resource contention. This configuration is suitable for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, lightweight machine learning inference using small models, and general-purpose compute tasks where a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio is optimal.
